issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the Y-state preparation function: the problem statement specifies a function named `_make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None`, but both the template repository and the solution repository define and use `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (no leading underscore). This mismatch can confuse students about which function to implement and cause tests or autograders to fail if they expect one name but the other is present.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update the problem statement to request `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (remove the leading underscore) so it matches the template and solution. Alternative fix: add a thin wrapper `_make_y_state` in the template (and solution/tests if needed) that simply calls `make_y_state(...)`, or rename `make_y_state` to `_make_y_state` in both template and solution and update any references/tests accordingly. Ensure tests and documentation reference the same identifier.

issues.description: The problem statement asks for a function named `_make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (preparing a noisy |Y> resource state), while both the template and the solution define the function as `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (no leading underscore). These three identifiers refer to the same conceptual operation (preparing a noisy |Y> resource state). The naming mismatch makes it unclear which identifier students should implement and which name tests will reference, increasing friction and risking test failures or confusion about whether to add a leading underscore or not.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Recommended: update the problem statement to request make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None (remove the leading underscore) so the task text, template stub, and solution all use the same name. Alternatively, if a leading underscore is intentional, rename the function in the template and solution to `_make_y_state` or add an alias `_make_y_state = make_y_state` to the template so tests and instructions align.
